greek-story-aristophanes-knights-first-a.name: Private Supper Tally
greek-story-aristophanes-knights-first-a.author: greek-story-aristophanes-knights-first
greek-story-aristophanes-knights-first-a.seed: A tally of the households allowed to draw flour from Demos’s pantry.

claims.text: The Paphlagonian keeps Demos’s pantry key and issues supper only to the names on his tally.

greek-story-aristophanes-clouds-first-an.name: Counter-Plea Tablet
greek-story-aristophanes-clouds-first-an.author: greek-story-aristophanes-clouds-first
greek-story-aristophanes-clouds-first-an.seed: The Thinkery’s argument about the horses, copied by a son who means to apply it to the bread.

claims.text: Strepsiades disputes the horse bill and his son claims the household’s loaf under the same argument.

greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-first-ans.name: The Dog’s Impounded Plate
greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-first-ans.author: greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-first
greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-first-ans.seed: Philocleon keeps the plate by his breakfast with an evidence label tied around it.

claims.text: Philocleon labels the dog’s full plate as evidence after sealing the conviction jar.

greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-second-an.name: The Dog’s Licked Bowl
greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-second-an.seed: The dog licked it clean after acquittal. Bdelycleon will put it away for the next meal.

greek-story-aristophanes-peace-first-ans.name: Rimstone Wedge
greek-story-aristophanes-peace-first-ans.seed: An oak wedge the farmers drove under the first stone before pulling on Trygaeus’s line.

greek-story-aristophanes-peace-second-an.name: Hermes’s Passage Token
greek-story-aristophanes-peace-second-an.author: greek-story-aristophanes-peace-second
greek-story-aristophanes-peace-second-an.seed: The token Hermes gave the farmers after taking their line as his fee.

claims.text: Hermes accepted the hauling rope as payment for letting the farmers approach Peace’s pit.

greek-story-aristophanes-birds-first-ans.name: Smoke Gate Pass
greek-story-aristophanes-birds-first-ans.author: greek-story-aristophanes-birds-first
greek-story-aristophanes-birds-first-ans.seed: Peisthetaerus’s first pass after the builders strung the smoke gate.

claims.text: Peisthetaerus requires even the gods to present a pass at the smoke gate.

greek-story-aristophanes-birds-second-an.name: The Sparrows’ Speaking Sprig
greek-story-aristophanes-birds-second-an.seed: The sparrows bring this to mark their turn and ask the Hoopoe to tie it to the council perch.

greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-firs.name: Empty Pay Wagon Tally
greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-firs.author: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-first
greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-firs.seed: The treasury clerk’s tally for an army wagon that leaves without a single coin.

claims.text: Lysistrata withheld the army chest and the pay wagon left empty.

greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-fi.name: Festival Speakers’ Roll
greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-fi.author: greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-first
greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-fi.seed: The First Woman leaves the speakers’ roll beside Agathon’s gown on the assembly bench.

claims.text: The First Woman restored the speaking turn Mnesilochus interrupted and kept Agathon’s gown before the assembly.

greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-first-ans.name: Aeschylus’s Chorus Staff
greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-first-ans.seed: A staff Aeschylus tapped against the landing to test the marching beat before departure.

greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-second-an.name: Complaint Against Charon’s Fare
greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-second-an.author: greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-second
greek-story-aristophanes-frogs-second-an.seed: The first few lines of Euripides’s speech against the ferry fare, scratched on a wax tablet.

claims.text: Euripides paid Charon for the Athens crossing and challenged the price from the bow.

greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-s.name: Tomorrow’s Barley Reserve
greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-s.author: greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-second
greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-s.seed: A sealed sack with a tally for the people who need to bake tomorrow.

claims.text: Chremes measured out barley for the next day’s bakers after the neighbor brought his grain.

greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-first-an.name: Chremylus’s Sowing Seed
greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-first-an.seed: The last seed Chremylus bought with the coin. Take it to him for the final furrow.

greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-second-a.name: Grain Surety Seal
greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-second-a.author: greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-second
greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-second-a.seed: The informer’s seal hangs on the sack of grain held while his claim is heard.

claims.text: The informer filed his claim and the grain remains held as surety while Chremylus’s field waits.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wasps-second
choices.text: Bdelycleon sets the bowl by the dog’s bed for breakfast and moves the jury jars out of its reach.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-birds-second
choices.text: The Hoopoe ties the sprig to the council perch and gives the sparrows the first speaking turn.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-first
choices.text: The magistrate sent a wagon for the army’s pay. With the key in my hands I can keep the chest locked. Give it to Lampito if you want her to pledge one chest to hospitality. She can share a loaf now with whoever is at the table.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-first
choices.text: Lysistrata keeps the Treasury Key and sends the army’s pay wagon away empty.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-second
choices.text: Lampito sets the Treasury Key on the coalition’s table and pledges one chest for hospitality during the talks.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-lysistrata-second
choices.text: Lampito breaks the loaf for those at the table and keeps the audience on the steps open a while longer.
choices.summary: Lampito shared Bread at the treasury steps and kept the audience open longer.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-thesmophoria-second
choices.text: Mnesilochus agrees to tell Euripides in person that the assembly expects him to answer under his own name.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-assemblywomen-first
choices.label: Give Bread for the common table
choices.text: Praxagora sets the Bread on the common table and enters it in the register for anyone who needs a meal.

choices.subject: greek-story-aristophanes-wealth-first
choices.text: Chremylus scatters the last seed in the far furrow and rakes the earth over it.
